subject.title: fix(codex): fail-closed on unknown item statuses and warn on dropped notifications

question: Should OpenClaw treat every explicit unknown Codex item status as failed by default, and which candidate PR should carry the canonical router-owned fix?
rationale: Current upstream enums are fully covered, but fail-closed behavior defines a future-protocol compatibility policy and the open candidate PRs use different correlation rules and ownership boundaries.

options.title: Approve fail-closed with router repair
options.body: Choose one candidate, preserve known and missing-status behavior, and require the stale-turn warning at the router’s actual drop boundary.

options.title: Narrow to projector-owned changes
options.body: Land only unknown-status and unknown-method handling, leaving cross-turn diagnostics to a separate router-owned follow-up.

options.title: Retain fail-open compatibility
options.body: Keep unknown explicit statuses as successful completion and accept the risk of false-success protocol drift.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed with router repair
recommendation.body: Choose one candidate, preserve known and missing-status behavior, and require the stale-turn warning at the router’s actual drop boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Current history shows they introduced and hardened the Codex harness and recently merged adjacent projector work.
